task_title: CI Recovery: exclude url from blocker fingerprint

plan_review.notes: Approved with changes (no blocking issues). Alt A (regex-normalize CI/workflow URLs instead of dropping) rejected: brittle across GitHub URL shapes, duplicates identity logic at each producer site. Alt B (per-kind semantic field whitelist) rejected: bigger refactor, not warranted for this incident (only justified if more volatile-field exceptions accumulate). Alt C (fix only in reconcile.mjs blocker construction) rejected: misses the ci-retrigger path and breaks the normalizeBlockers/fingerprint separation of display-vs-semantic metadata. Chosen: exclude url from blockerFingerprint centrally (same pattern as the existing line exclusion) -- divergence=minor (alternatives considered, none beat the chosen design, but follow-up coverage was added). Concern 1 (non-blocking): ci-retrigger kind was not directly regression-tested -- resolved by adding a dedicated ci-retrigger URL-drift fingerprint-stability test in state.test.mjs. Concern 2 (suggestion): integration tests did not assert the rewritten state carries the freshest live url for display -- resolved by adding an explicit assertion in the cycle-2/3 PR #1809 integration test that finalState.blockers[0].url reflects the latest live check-run url. No new correctness risk found (url is confirmed non-semantic for all present blocker kinds); no weakening of ownership safety, reaper ceilings, or trusted-workflow boundaries; no architecture change warranted.

rounds.notes: Single-model code review of full diff (state.mjs fix, state.test.mjs, reconcile.test.mjs). Verified all 125 reconcile.test.mjs tests + 43 state.test.mjs tests pass. No findings across correctness, data flow, API/compat, collision risk, security, wiring, performance, regression coverage, scope/apple estimate, or reviewer-persona categories.
